source: upload-your-own-music market (cloud music lockers, self-hosted servers, mainstream streamers' upload features)
method: WebSearch to discover; each reachable page fetched once (>=3.5 s apart) with python urllib/curl through the configured proxy; official APIs (iTunes Lookup, App Store reviews RSS, HN Algolia) and shallow git clones of official docs/README repos where the website was blocked. Quotes were extracted programmatically from raw responses and machine-checked as exact substrings of the tag-stripped, whitespace-collapsed text.
caveat: Most vendor sites (Google support, YouTube blog, Apple support, plex.tv, navidrome.org, deezer, ibroadcast, vox.rocks) are blocked by this session's egress policy, so several official facts come from HN users quoting the official text (source_kind=user-quoting-official) or from HN submission titles (source_kind=news-index). The 'leads_unverified' block is from search summaries only and must not be quoted.

failures.claim: Users dislike YouTube Music matching songs in their library with random YouTube audio.
failures.reason: Quote is not the linked commenter's words: in item 42534743 it is a '>'-quoted line from the parent comment (item 42531650). The linked comment itself says the matching 'stopped happening' and 'You can also turn off this functionality all together in the settings', so the present-tense claim 'Users dislike YouTube Music matching...' leaves out context that undercuts it. Fix: link the parent comment and note that the reply says the feature can be turned off.

failures.claim: Deezer is one of the few mainstream streamers that lets users upload their own MP3s (user report; Deezer's help page is unreachable from here).

failures.claim: Plexamp's current iOS App Store version was released on 2025-07-14, so the iOS app has had no update for over a year as of 2026-10-04.
failures.reason: The quote is a raw iTunes Lookup API JSON fragment. It does not appear on the linked apps.apple.com page. The fact itself is true: the page shows 'Version 4.12.4' dated 07/14/2025, and https://itunes.apple.com/lookup?id=1500797510&country=us contains the exact string. Fix: link the lookup API URL, or quote the page's version/date text.

failures.claim: Plexamp's Google Play listing shows in-app purchases ranging up to $949.99 per item.
failures.reason: The quote '$0.99 - $949.99 per item' is not on the linked URL (no hl/gl parameters) as served now. It is present only on https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=tv.plex.labs.plexamp&hl=en_US&gl=US, in the embedded page data. Fix: use that URL.

failures.claim: In March 2025 Plex ended free remote streaming and roughly doubled the Plex Pass price (HN submission linking the official plex.tv blog post, which is unreachable from here).
failures.reason: Overstated: the quote is an HN submitter's own headline, not Plex's words or a publisher's. The linked plex.tv post's slug is 'important-2025-plex-updates', and nothing else on the HN page backs the details (7 comments, none on pricing). The claim turns that headline into dated fact ('In March 2025 Plex ended free remote streaming and roughly doubled the price'). The same file's leads block dates the new pricing 'From 29 Apr 2025' and notes the remote paywall applied to video, not Plexamp music. Fix: frame it as 'an HN submission (2025-03-21) titled ...' or source the official post.

failures.claim: What users pay Plex for is easy remote access. Self-hosted connectivity is the hard part for non-experts.
failures.reason: Overstated: one user's comment is generalized into 'What users pay Plex for is easy remote access'. The quote says Plex handles 'the IP stuff for remote play, which is the tough part for me'. Fix: attribute it to one user ('a Plex user says Plex handles the remote-access networking they find hardest when self-hosting').

failures.claim: play:Sub is a paid ($4.99) iOS client for Subsonic servers.
